description: Create src/pipeline/ module with SearchPipeline class that orchestrates the complete filtering and search workflow. Integrate BinaryFilter (pre and post), VSMSearcher, and load dataset for metadata enrichment. Implement search method that: (1) applies pre-filters (year + primary_category) to get candidates, (2) runs VSM search with candidates, (3) applies post-filters (authors + categories) to results, (4) returns enriched results with full metadata. Add CLI with argparse for interactive searching.
steps: Create src/pipeline/search_pipeline.py with SearchPipeline class. In __init__: instantiate VSMSearcher, BinaryFilter, load dataset parquet (pd.read_parquet) for metadata access

Implement search(query, year_range=None, primary_categories=None, authors=None, all_categories=None, top_k=10) method following this sequence: (1) Call bf.get_pre_filter_candidates(year_range, primary_categories) to get candidate doc indices (or None for all docs). (2) Call vsm.search(query, candidates=candidates, top_k=top_k) to get initial results. (3) Extract doc_ids from results, apply bf.apply_post_filters(doc_ids, authors, all_categories). (4) Filter results list to only include post-filtered doc_ids. (5) Enrich each result with full metadata from dataset (id, title, abstract, authors, categories, primary_category, year). (6) Return list of dicts with metadata + score + rank fields

Add CLI using argparse: python -m src.pipeline.search_pipeline QUERY --year-min Y --year-max Y --primary-categories cat1 cat2 --authors a1 a2 --all-categories c1 c2 --top N. Format output to show rank, score, title, authors, year, categories
Handle edge cases: empty results at any stage, no filters specified (search all docs), null metadata values
acceptance_criteria: SearchPipeline can be instantiated and loads all required components without errors
search() with no filters returns same results as direct VSM search
search() with year_range=(2020, 2022) only returns papers from 2020-2022
search() with primary_categories=['cs.AI'] only returns papers with primary_category='cs.AI'
search() with authors=['smith'] returns papers where any author name contains 'smith' (case-insensitive)
Combining pre-filters and post-filters works correctly (intersection logic)
CLI runs successfully and displays formatted results
verification: C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe -c "from src.pipeline import SearchPipeline; sp = SearchPipeline(); results = sp.search('graph neural network', top_k=5); print(f'Found {len(results)} results'); print(results[0] if results else 'No results')"
findings: Successfully implemented search pipeline orchestrating BinaryFilter pre/post-filtering with VSM search. Implementation creates src/pipeline/ module with SearchPipeline class that: (1) applies pre-filters (year_range + primary_categories) using BinaryFilter.get_pre_filter_candidates(), (2) passes candidates to VSM.search(), (3) applies post-filters (authors + categories) to results, (4) enriches results with full metadata from dataset. CLI implemented with argparse supporting all filter parameters (--year-min, --year-max, --primary-categories, --authors, --all-categories, --top). Handles edge cases including empty results at any stage, no filters specified, null metadata values, and VSM index subset (filters candidates to VSM doc range). All 9 SearchPipeline tests passing. Note: VSM index (1000 docs) is subset of full dataset (380k docs), so pre-filtering must constrain candidates to VSM range to avoid index errors. Implementation correctly handles this by filtering candidates where doc_idx < vsm.n_docs.
